## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the penalty for not filing Form 5472?

The IRS instructions state a USD 25,000 penalty for failing to file Form 5472 on time and in the required manner. It applies per form, per year, and a substantially incomplete form is treated as a failure to file.

### Is there an additional penalty if I ignore an IRS notice?

Yes. If the failure continues more than 90 days after the IRS notifies you, an additional USD 25,000 applies for each related party for each 30-day period, or part of one, after the 90 days.

### I have missed Form 5472 for several years. What should I do?

Reconstruct every owner transaction since formation, check whether the IRS has already contacted you, then prepare the pro forma Form 1120 and Form 5472 for each missing year with a reasonable cause statement. The IRS delinquent international return procedures apply only if you are not under examination and have not been contacted; have a professional confirm the route.

### Can the penalty be waived?

It may be abated for reasonable cause and not willful neglect, but the IRS can still assess it without considering the statement, and ignorance of the rule is commonly reported to be a weak ground. Whether first-time abatement applies to Form 5472 is disputed by practitioners, so we do not rely on it. No waiver is guaranteed.

### Can a foreign-owned single-member LLC e-file Form 5472?

No. The IRS instructions say a foreign-owned US disregarded entity cannot file Form 5472 electronically. The pro forma Form 1120 with Form 5472 attached is faxed or mailed to the IRS PIN Unit in Ogden, Utah, using the details in the current instructions.

# LLP Form 8 and Form 11 Due Dates: FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27

Published November 18, 2026[CA Mehul Agrawal](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/about#mehul-agrawal)Agrawal Khandelwal & Associates LLP

TL;DR

- **Next due dates (FY 2026-27):** Form 11 by **May 30, 2027** and Form 8 by **October 30, 2027**. The same dates apply every year.
- **Form 11** was due **May 30, 2026** and **Form 8** was due **October 30, 2026** for FY 2025-26. We found no extension for LLPs as of November 18, 2026.
- MCA General Circular 05/2026 relaxed additional fees only for company forms AOC-4 and MGT-7, not LLP forms.
- The old **Rs 100 per day** late fee was replaced from April 1, 2022 by a table of multiples of the normal fee, with a daily component only beyond 360 days.
- An LLP audit applies above Rs 25 lakh contribution or Rs 40 lakh turnover. The income tax return (ITR-5) and any tax audit are separate.
- From March 31, 2026, **DIR-3 KYC is filed once every three years, by June 30**, plus within 30 days of any change in contact details. Backlog filings should be cleared before any strike off or closure.

An LLP has two annual MCA filings and no AGM, which is why many partners forget them. Both carry per-form late fees that grow with delay, and a dormant LLP still has to file. This guide covers the FY 2025-26 dates, the current late fee structure, the income tax side, DIR-3 KYC and what happens if you stop filing. For registration, see our [LLP registration guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/llp-registration-process-cost-india-2026).

## The two MCA filings and their dates for FY 2025-26

Form 11 is the annual return and Form 8 is the statement of account and solvency. Both are filed every year, even if the LLP had no business.

| Form | What it is | Due date for FY 2025-26 | Extended? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Form 11 | Annual return of partners and activity | May 30, 2026 (60 days from year end) | No extension found |
| Form 8 | Statement of account and solvency | October 30, 2026 (30 days after six months from year end) | No extension found |

**For FY 2026-27** (the year ending March 31, 2027), the same rules give **Form 11 by May 30, 2027** and **Form 8 by October 30, 2027**. Check the MCA portal nearer the date for any extension.

## Did MCA extend any LLP date for FY 2025-26?

As of November 18, 2026, we found no extension for LLP Form 11 or Form 8. MCA General Circular 05/2026 (October 24, 2026) relaxed additional fees only for company forms AOC-4 and MGT-7. It does not cover LLPs. If you have not filed Form 8 yet, it is already late. Check the MCA LLP circulars page before relying on any extension someone mentions.

## Late fees: the daily Rs 100 charge is gone

Older guides still say Rs 100 per day. From April 1, 2022 the LLP (Amendment) Rules, 2022 replaced that with a table of additional fees based on a multiple of the normal fee. The multiple depends on how long you are late, and a small LLP pays a lower multiple. Two independent guides publish the same structure, reproduced below. Confirm it in the MCA fee calculator before relying on exact amounts.

| Delay | Small LLP | Other LLP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up to 15 days | 1x | 1x |
| 15 to 30 days | 2x | 4x |
| 30 to 60 days | 4x | 8x |
| 60 to 90 days | 6x | 12x |
| 90 to 180 days | 10x | 20x |
| 180 to 360 days | 15x | 30x |
| Beyond 360 days | 15x plus Rs 10 per day | 30x plus Rs 20 per day |

## What is the normal fee?

The normal fee depends on contribution. Published guides list Rs 50 up to Rs 1 lakh, Rs 100 up to Rs 5 lakh, Rs 150 up to Rs 10 lakh, Rs 200 up to Rs 25 lakh, Rs 400 up to Rs 1 crore and Rs 600 above. A small LLP means contribution up to Rs 25 lakh and turnover up to Rs 40 lakh. Each form is charged separately, so a long-pending LLP pays for both forms and for every year.

Separately, the LLP Act contains penalty provisions for default by the LLP and its designated partners. Those sit on top of the additional fees, and we have not quoted amounts because guides disagree on the cap.

## Audit, income tax return and tax audit for LLPs

A statutory audit of the LLP's accounts is required where contribution exceeds Rs 25 lakh or turnover exceeds Rs 40 lakh. Below that, accounts must still be maintained and a solvency statement signed in Form 8.

For income tax, an LLP files ITR-5. If a tax audit applies (for example because turnover crosses the Section 44AB threshold, a separate test from the LLP Act audit), audit-case dates apply. For AY 2026-27, the CBDT press release of September 28, 2026 extended the audit report to October 21, 2026 and the audit-case return to November 21, 2026, with Form 3CEB cases excluded. Read our [audit case ITR due date post](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog) and confirm for your facts. LLP, income tax and GST filings are separate, and one does not substitute for another.

## DIR-3 KYC for designated partners

Designated partners who hold a DIN must file DIR-3 KYC. Since March 31, 2026 this is once every three financial years, by June 30 (a director who filed in FY 2025-26 is next due by June 30, 2028), plus within 30 days of any change in mobile number, email or address. Missing it deactivates the DIN, and published guides report a fee of Rs 5,000 to reactivate. A deactivated DIN blocks the partner from signing MCA forms, including Form 8 and Form 11. One source says a partner holding only a DPIN may be treated differently, so check each partner's status. See the [DSC and DIN guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/dsc-din-application-director-guide).

## If you stop filing: consequences

Additional fees keep growing, and past 360 days they carry a daily component. Pending defaults also get in the way of closing the LLP: the ROC expects backlog Form 8 and Form 11 to be filed before a voluntary strike off (Form 24). The ROC can also strike off an LLP that is not carrying on business or not filing, under Section 75 of the LLP Act, which makes bank accounts and property dealings difficult and can require a court route to restore. Whether you want to keep the LLP or close it, filing the backlog is usually cheaper than leaving it.

## A simple yearly calendar for your LLP

Keep books through the year, finalise accounts and the solvency statement, file DIR-3 KYC by June 30 in its three-year cycle, file Form 11 by May 30 and Form 8 by October 30, and file the ITR and any tax audit on the dates that apply. If you are unsure about the audit threshold or have an old default, see our [compliance calendar](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/startup-compliance-calendar-year-1-3) or [company incorporation and compliance services](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/company-incorporation).

**Official sources:** Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008; LLP Rules, 2009 as amended by the LLP (Amendment) Rules, 2022 (additional fees); MCA General Circular 05/2026 dated October 24, 2026 (company forms only). See [Ministry of Corporate Affairs](https://www.mca.gov.in/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What are the due dates for LLP Form 8 and Form 11 for FY 2025-26?

Form 11 was due on May 30, 2026 and Form 8 on October 30, 2026. Both are filed every year, even if the LLP did no business.

### Has MCA extended LLP Form 8 or Form 11 for FY 2025-26?

We found no extension as of November 18, 2026. MCA General Circular 05/2026 relaxed additional fees only for company forms AOC-4 and MGT-7. Check the MCA portal for any later LLP circular.

### What is the late fee for LLP Form 8 and Form 11?

Since April 1, 2022 the additional fee is a multiple of the normal fee that rises with the delay, and a small LLP pays a lower multiple. Beyond 360 days a daily amount is added. The old flat Rs 100 per day no longer applies. Confirm exact amounts in the MCA fee calculator.

### Is an audit compulsory for an LLP?

A statutory audit is required if contribution exceeds Rs 25 lakh or turnover exceeds Rs 40 lakh. A tax audit under the Income Tax Act is a separate test based on turnover and other conditions.

### What are the LLP Form 8 and Form 11 due dates for FY 2026-27?

Form 11 is due by May 30, 2027 and Form 8 by October 30, 2027, following the same 60-day and six-months-plus-30-days rules that apply every year.

### Do designated partners need to file DIR-3 KYC?

Yes, if they hold a DIN. From March 31, 2026 the annual filing was replaced by a filing once every three financial years, due by June 30, plus a filing within 30 days of any change in mobile number, email or address. A director who filed in FY 2025-26 is next due by June 30, 2028. Missing it deactivates the DIN. A partner with only a DPIN may be treated differently, so check the status.

### What happens if an LLP does not file annual returns?

Additional fees keep accruing, DINs may be deactivated, and the ROC can strike off the LLP under Section 75 of the LLP Act. Backlog filings are normally needed before a voluntary strike off.

US Cross-Border

# Setting Up an Indian Subsidiary for a US C-Corp: Steps and Compliance

Published November 18, 2026[CA Mehul Agrawal](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/about#mehul-agrawal)Agrawal Khandelwal & Associates LLP

TL;DR

- Most service and software businesses can be 100% owned by a US parent under the automatic route. Restricted sectors and land-border investors need approval.
- A private company needs two members, so a nominee holds one share for the parent.
- One director must have stayed in India 182 days in the previous financial year (s.149(3)).
- Report the foreign investment on FC-GPR within 30 days of allotment.
- Services to the US parent need arm's-length pricing and, above the threshold, Form 3CEB.
- Keep contracts and key decisions in the US to limit permanent establishment risk.

Running a US LLC or C-Corp from India?

Our team prepares your US filings and our US partner reviews and files them, while we keep your Indian side (ITR, FEMA, transfer pricing) in step.

[Book a US compliance call](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/consult?topic=us-cross-border)[See US packages](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/us-cross-border#packages)

A US C-Corp that wants an engineering, support or sales team in India usually does it through a wholly owned Indian private limited company. The set-up is straightforward. The compliance that follows is where US parents get caught, especially on FEMA reporting and transfer pricing.

## FDI Route and Eligibility

Most service and software businesses fall under the automatic route, which needs no prior government or RBI approval. A few sectors are restricted or need approval, and investors from countries sharing a land border with India need government approval under Press Note 3. Check your sector against the current FDI policy before incorporating. Our [foreign subsidiary registration guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/foreign-subsidiary-registration-india-fdi) and [FDI routes guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/fdi-in-india-routes-compliance-guide) cover this in detail.

Where the US parent is itself owned by Indian-resident founders, the overseas investment rules decide who can hold it. See [the startup triangle structure](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/startup-triangle-structure-llp-us-c-corp-indian-subsidiary) for the common LLP-held set-up.

## Two Shareholders and the Nominee

A private limited company needs at least two members. A US parent therefore holds almost all the shares and a nominee, often a director or a related individual, holds one share on its behalf, with a declaration that the nominee holds for the parent. Record the nominee holding properly. Do not leave it informal, since the registers and filings need the right beneficial ownership details.

## Resident Director

Section 149(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires at least one director who has stayed in India for at least 182 days in the previous financial year. It is counted over the financial year, not a calendar year. In practice parents either appoint a trusted India-based manager or use a professional director. Pick someone who understands the duties, since a director carries statutory liability.

## Incorporation Sequence

- Digital signature certificates and director identification numbers for the proposed directors (see [DSC and DIN](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/dsc-din-application-director-guide)).
- Name reservation and SPICe+ incorporation, with the parent's documents apostilled or notarised as required.
- PAN and TAN, and GST registration if the Indian company will invoice.
- Open the company bank account and remit the share capital from the US parent.
- Allot shares to the parent and the nominee.

Foreign documents from the US must be properly authenticated for Indian filings, so start that early.

## FC-GPR Within 30 Days of Allotment

Foreign investment received for shares must be reported to RBI on Form FC-GPR through the FIRMS portal within 30 days of allotment, with a valuation certificate and supporting documents. Funds should come in through normal banking channels, and shares generally need to be allotted within the permitted window after the money arrives. A late filing is regularised through the RBI late submission fee, so build the date into your closing checklist. The company also files the annual FLA return once it has foreign investment.

## Transfer Pricing on Services to the US Parent

When the Indian company provides services to its US parent, that is an international transaction with an associated enterprise, and it must be priced at arm's length. Where the value of such transactions crosses the prescribed threshold, the Indian company files an accountant's report on Form 3CEB and keeps transfer pricing documentation. Our [Form 3CEB guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/form-3ceb-transfer-pricing-audit-report) covers due dates and penalties. A cost-plus model is the usual starting point for captive service companies, and the mark-up must be supportable by a benchmarking study, not chosen casually.

## Indian Corporate Tax Options

An Indian private limited company owned by a foreign parent is still a domestic company for tax purposes. It can pay tax at the regular rate (25% or 30% depending on turnover, plus surcharge and cess) or opt for the lower concessional regime, which has a 22% base rate and gives up certain exemptions and incentives, bringing the effective rate to roughly 25% after surcharge and cess. The concessional regime is a one-way election, and section numbers have changed under the Income Tax Act, 2025, so confirm the current section and rate when you decide. Dividends paid to the US parent attract Indian withholding tax, which the India-US treaty can reduce. See [the India-US DTAA guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/india-us-dtaa-guide).

## Permanent Establishment Risk

A subsidiary is not automatically a permanent establishment of its parent. It becomes a risk when the Indian team habitually concludes contracts for the parent, the parent's executives run the business from India, or the subsidiary acts as a dependent agent. The India-US treaty also has a services permanent establishment test based on the presence of personnel. Keep contracts signed in the US, document who takes decisions and where, and avoid treating the Indian entity as a branch. Also watch where the US company is actually managed, since place of effective management can make a foreign company Indian-resident if control sits in India.

## Annual Compliance Checklist

- Statutory audit, AOC-4 and MGT-7 filings (see [annual ROC filing](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/annual-roc-filing-aoc4-mgt7-dir3-kyc)).
- Income tax return, advance tax, and TDS compliance.
- GST returns if registered.
- FLA return and any FEMA reporting for fresh investment.
- Form 3CEB and transfer pricing documentation.

If you are still deciding whether the parent should be a Delaware company at all, read [our flip structure guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/india-to-us-flip-structure-guide). For the wider picture, see [our startup advisory](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/startups) and [US cross-border services](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/us-cross-border).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can a US company own 100% of an Indian private limited company?

Yes in most sectors under the automatic route. A private limited company needs two members, so a nominee holds one share on behalf of the parent. Some sectors are restricted or need approval, so check the sector first.

### Does the Indian subsidiary need a resident director?

Yes. Section 149(3) of the Companies Act, 2013 requires at least one director who has stayed in India for at least 182 days in the previous financial year.

### When is FC-GPR due?

Within 30 days of allotment of shares to the foreign investor, filed on the RBI FIRMS portal. A late filing is regularised through the RBI late submission fee.

### Is Form 3CEB required for services to the US parent?

If the value of international transactions with the parent crosses the prescribed threshold, yes. The Indian company files the accountant's report on Form 3CEB and keeps documentation showing the price is at arm's length. Check the current threshold and due date at filing time.

### What tax rate does the Indian subsidiary pay?

It is taxed as a domestic company: the regular 25% or 30% depending on turnover, or the concessional regime at a 22% base rate that gives up certain deductions. Surcharge and cess apply on top. Confirm the current section and rate under the Income Tax Act, 2025 when you choose.

### Does an Indian subsidiary create a permanent establishment for the US parent?

Not automatically. Risk arises if the Indian team habitually concludes contracts for the parent, if the parent is managed from India, or if the subsidiary acts as a dependent agent. Contract signing and decision-making should be kept and documented in the US.

Startup Compliance

# MSME-1 Half-Yearly Return: Who Files, Due Dates and Penalty

Published November 18, 2026[CA Mehul Agrawal](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/about#mehul-agrawal)Agrawal Khandelwal & Associates LLP

TL;DR

- **MSME-1** is a half-yearly return for companies that have **outstanding payments to micro or small enterprise suppliers for more than 45 days**.
- Due dates: **October 31** for April to September, and **April 30** for October to March. The April to September 2026 return was due October 31, 2026.
- If no dues to micro and small suppliers are pending beyond 45 days, there is **no return to file**. It is not a nil-return form.
- The updated form on the MCA V3 portal asks for amounts paid within and after 45 days and the **reasons for delay**.
- Section 405(4) penalty: **Rs 20,000** on the company plus Rs 1,000 a day of continuing failure, capped at **Rs 3 lakh**. Officers in default are also liable.
- Delayed payment also has a **tax cost**: see Section 43B(h), covered in our separate post.

Starting a company in India?

We incorporate your private limited company and run its first year of ROC compliance (INC-20A, first board meeting, auditor appointment, AOC-4 and MGT-7).

[Book a free startup call](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/consult?topic=startups)[See the startup package](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/startups#packages)

A startup that buys from small vendors, such as a freelancer, a printer, a small manufacturer or a software agency registered as a micro or small enterprise, has a legal clock on every invoice. If payment drifts past 45 days, two things can happen: the company may owe interest to the supplier, and it may have to report the delay to the Registrar in Form MSME-1. Founders often meet both for the first time in an audit.

## Who Must File MSME-1

The requirement applies to a company that has obtained goods or services from **micro and small enterprises** and whose payment to any such supplier has been **outstanding for more than 45 days** from the date of acceptance of the goods or services. It rests on the payment rules in Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006, and the reporting rule in Section 405 of the Companies Act read with the MCA specified companies order. Medium enterprises are not covered.

Two points are easy to miss. First, the 45 days apply even where the written agreement says 60 or 90 days, because the statute caps the credit period at 45 days where there is a written agreement, and at 15 days where there is none. Second, MSME-1 is filed only if such a delay actually exists. It is not an annual nil-return.

## Due Dates

| Half-year | Covers | Due date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First half | April to September | October 31 |
| Second half | October to March | April 30 |

The return for April to September 2026 was due on October 31, 2026. We did not find a general MCA extension for it. If you missed it, file now. The next return, for October 2026 to March 2027, is due on April 30, 2027. Add both dates to your [startup compliance calendar](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/startup-compliance-calendar-year-1-3).

## What the Return Contains

The return asks for details of each micro or small supplier with dues pending beyond 45 days: the supplier name, PAN, the amount due, the date from which it has been due, and the reason for non-payment. The updated format on the MCA V3 portal also asks for amounts paid within 45 days and amounts paid after 45 days. The Ministry of MSME reiterated the requirement through a notification dated March 25, 2025. We found no sign of a further format change for 2025-26, but check the form on the portal before you file, since MCA revises forms without much notice.

## Penalty for Non-Filing

Section 405 of the Companies Act provides penalties for failing to file the return or for filing incorrect information. Under Section 405(4), the company is liable to a penalty of Rs 20,000, with a further Rs 1,000 for each day the failure continues, subject to a maximum of Rs 3 lakh, and officers in default are also liable. This is not theoretical: Registrars of Companies issued adjudication orders under Section 454 in January 2026 for MSME-1 returns filed years late. We found no filing fee for the form itself.

The larger cost is usually interest. Under the MSMED Act, a buyer who delays payment owes compound interest at three times the bank rate notified by the RBI, and that interest is not deductible. A supplier can also complain through the MSME Samadhaan portal.

## The Tax Link: Section 43B(h)

For income tax, a payment to a micro or small enterprise that is outstanding beyond the permitted 15 or 45 days at year end is deductible only when actually paid. This can raise taxable income in the year of default. We explain it in full in [Section 43B(h) and MSME payment disallowance](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog). MSME-1 and Section 43B(h) rest on the same 45-day idea, so one supplier ledger can serve both.

## A Simple Process for a Startup

1. Ask every vendor for their Udyam registration and note whether they are micro, small or medium. See our [Udyam registration guide](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/blog/startup-india-registration-vs-dpiit-recognition-what-is-the-difference).
2. Put the 45-day limit in your vendor agreements and the payables calendar.
3. Two weeks before each half-year end, run an ageing of payables to micro and small suppliers.
4. If any dues are past 45 days at the end of the half-year and not paid, file MSME-1 with the reasons.
5. Clear the oldest dues before March 31 to protect the Section 43B(h) deduction.

If you are unsure which of your vendors counts as micro or small, our [startup advisory](https://agrawalkhandelwal.com/startups) team can review your payables and set up the checks.

**Official sources:** Section 405 of the Companies Act, 2013; Section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006; Ministry of MSME notification of March 25, 2025. See [Ministry of Corporate Affairs](https://www.mca.gov.in/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Who has to file MSME-1?

A company that has bought goods or services from micro or small enterprises and has payments outstanding for more than 45 days from acceptance. If there are no such dues at the end of a half-year, no return is needed.

### What are the due dates for MSME-1?

October 31 for the April to September half-year and April 30 for the October to March half-year. The April to September 2026 return was due October 31, 2026, and the next is due April 30, 2027.

### Is MSME-1 required if there are no delayed payments?

No. It is filed only where dues to micro or small suppliers are pending beyond 45 days. It is not a nil-return form.

### What is the penalty for not filing MSME-1?

Under Section 405(4) of the Companies Act, the company faces a penalty of Rs 20,000, plus Rs 1,000 for each day the failure continues, up to Rs 3 lakh. Officers in default are also liable. Registrars have issued adjudication orders under Section 454 for delayed MSME-1 filings.

### Did the MSME-1 format change in 2025-26?

The updated form on the MCA V3 portal asks for amounts paid within and after 45 days and reasons for delay, and the Ministry of MSME reiterated the requirement on March 25, 2025. We found no further change for 2025-26, but check the portal before filing.

### How is MSME-1 linked to Section 43B(h)?

Both use the 45-day rule. MSME-1 is a Companies Act reporting form, while Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act makes the expense deductible only on payment if the dues to a micro or small supplier remain unpaid at year end.
